dossier.public_summary: The 1-day dip is not a planet transit but the star's own 1.04-day spin, seen as strong spot flicker and a large brightness swing outside the dips. The dip depth almost doubles between sectors and the shape requires an implausibly low stellar density, pointing to the M dwarf's large spots or a grazing stellar companion, both ruled on-target. No planet can be inferred from the data.

reasons.why: The 1.04 d dip period is identical to the star's spot rotation period seen in every sector with amplitudes 24074-50188 ppm (~6% modulation). A large out-of-transit swing indicates ellipsoidal/spots from a close companion, not a planet.
reasons.value: rotation_d 1.042 vs signal_period_d 1.04188, ratio 0.9999; phase_curve amplitude_ppm 8296, ratio_to_depth 1.187, chi2 7307 dof 9

reasons.why: Depth varies by ~140% even within the same pipeline, inconsistent with a stable transiting planet. Modulation by stellar activity is expected when a spot harmonic mimics a transit.
reasons.value: sectors.p_constant 1.2e-81, depth_change_pct 136.8, sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source, SPOC 2-min p_constant 8.00e-40, TESS-SPOC p_constant 1.82e-44, per-sector depths 3508 to 10955 ppm

reasons.why: Transit shape and duration imply a stellar density much lower than the M dwarf, with ultra-high penalty pointing to the signal not being around a main-sequence star. This matches a grazing stellar eclipse on the active star.
reasons.value: star_density_penalty 25910, penalty_share 0.7437, duration ratio 1.54 (1.35 with Gaia FLAME), fit_b 8.802e-9, fit_log_density_ratio -2.224

reasons.why: The dip is on the target and no 1-pixel neighbour can produce it, ruling out a blended eclipsing binary; the false positive is intrinsic stellar variability / eclipsing binary on the target.
reasons.value: centroid verdict on_target, offset_arcsec 1.964, err_arcsec 1.449, offset_sigma 1.355, plausible_within_1px 0, could_cause_within_1px 0
